title: FocusBranch: Combinatorial Branch-and-Bound for $\ell_0$ Neural Network Robustness Verification
claim: A search procedure alternates bounding and branching over structured nodes, and falls back to an exact solver only for rare unresolved cases.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right flowchart with feedback loops and a dashed definition box
description: A single flowchart showing the verification loop. Inputs f, x*, and ε enter from the top and feed a blue 'Plan' box that samples nodes and chooses the starting level l_s and branching strategy R. An arrow labelled 'init worklist' leads to a central cream box, 'Dequeue o; BOUND(o)'. A self-loop labelled 'safe, continue' sits above that box. An arrow labelled 'worklist empty' goes to 'Verified' at the top right. A cycle runs between the central box and a green 'BRANCH(o)' box below it, with 'unknown, branchable' going down and 'enqueue child nodes' coming back up. The green box lists super node: covering design, and concrete node: upper shadow. An arrow labelled 'unknown, unbranchable' goes to a pink 'MILP fallback (rare)' box. A dotted 'infeasible' arrow returns from it, and 'feasible' leads to 'Adversarial Example'. A dashed box at bottom left defines the node as o := (S, l).
caption: Overview of FOCUSBRANCH. After choosing ls and R(ls) by sampling, FOCUSBRANCH runs branch-and-bound over node-constrained ℓ0-balls, branching via covering designs (super node) or upper shadows (concrete node). Unknown, unbranchable nodes fall back to MILP.
abstract: Verifying the local robustness of neural networks under $\ell_0$ perturbations is inherently combinatorial, as it must reason over all sparse subsets of $Îµ$ perturbed pixels. This paper presents FocusBranch, a combinatorial branch-and-bound framework for $\ell_0$ robustness verification. The key insight is to make the $\ell_0$-ball decomposable and branchable using a node abstraction, which consists of a focus pixel set $\mathcal{S}$ and a level $l$, permitting at most $Îµ-l$ pixels outside $\mathcal{S}$. This abstraction unifies two branching mechanisms: concrete nodes branch through upper shadows to fix additional perturbed locations, while super nodes branch through covering designs to cover many perturbation cases with fewer child nodes. FocusBranch proves node safety by concretizing linear relaxations over node-constrained $\ell_0$-balls and recursively branches on unknown nodes. Rather than relying on a fixed verification plan, it samples nodes across levels to estimate safe rates and costs, then selects a starting level and branching strategy predicted to minimize verification time. Experiments on fully connected and convolutional classifiers for MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 show that FocusBranch verifies $\ell_0$ robustness effectively across architectures and outperforms state-of-the-art verifiers. The code is available at: https://github.com/simpl-group/FocusBranch.
